Chapter 1: The River House

Rahim Mia lived in the old house beside the river. Everyone in the village called him Master Sahib, although he had retired.

“Will you still wait for me today?” Geeta asked.

Rahim Mia smiled and said, “Of course, Geeta; forgetting a promise is not the work of a good person.” Then he looked out the window and watched the monsoon clouds gather slowly while the distant boat disappeared into the mist.

✦ ✦ ✦

On 12 Baishakh 1432, they sat by the river with panta bhat and green chilies.

Chapter 2: The Promise

The following year Geeta returned, and Rahim Mia left the same blue umbrella beside the door.

“Master Sahib, did you recognize me?” Geeta said.

He answered, “How could I forget you? This river and this house were both waiting for you.” His voice held joy, but the shadow of an old farewell remained in his eyes.

✦ ✦ ✦

In the evening they shared panta bhat and remembered that day, 12 Baishakh; Rahim Mia knew that small promises are what hold the story of a long life together.
